name: Bilgai
overview: Bilgai was a male member of the tribe of Levi who served as an Aaronic priest. He is specifically noted in the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, with his name appearing at Nehemiah 10:8. His role as a priest connects him directly to the sacred duties established for the descendants of Aaron.
namesAndTitles: The name Bilgai means 'gleam' or 'smile,' reflecting a proper Hebrew name without indication that it was given by God. This meaning may suggest a positive or radiant character, though the biblical text does not elaborate beyond the name itself.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Bilgai as a descendant of Aaron, linking him to the priestly lineage. Beyond this inferred relationship, no additional family connections are recorded in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Bilgai’s significance lies in his role as an Aaronic priest who affixed his name to the covenant document in Nehemiah 10, demonstrating his commitment to the covenant renewal among the returned exiles. His inclusion among the priests highlights the continuity of the Levitical priesthood and their vital role in upholding the spiritual and communal obligations of Israel during the post-exilic period.
